findings.evidence: `def halfLinePrimitive` at line 58 with no `@[expose]`; grep of the file shows the only equations are the two half-line-conditional ones.
findings.fix: Add `theorem halfLinePrimitive_def (f : ℝ → ℝ) (t : ℝ) : halfLinePrimitive f t = ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..t, f (max x 0) := (rfl)` and use it in place of the `rw [halfLinePrimitive]` unfoldings.
findings.issue: `halfLinePrimitive`'s body is not `@[expose]`d (correct) but no unconditional defining equation is exported: only `halfLinePrimitive_eq_integral_of_nonneg` and `halfLinePrimitive_of_nonpos`. In-file proofs unfold with `rw [halfLinePrimitive]` (lines 73, 81, 91, 137), which downstream files cannot do.

findings.evidence: Line 128–129 `have hcontinuous : ContinuousOn (halfLinePrimitive f) (Ici 0) := ...`; grep for `continuous_primitive` in Integral.lean returns nothing.
findings.fix: Promote it to a named lemma `continuous_halfLinePrimitive (hf : ContinuousOn f (Ici 0)) : Continuous (halfLinePrimitive f)` — the `max` extension makes it continuous on all of ℝ — and use it in the `have`.
findings.issue: Continuity of `halfLinePrimitive f` is derived only inside a `have` in `isBernsteinFunction_halfLinePrimitive`. It needs nothing beyond `ContinuousOn f (Ici 0)`, yet a consumer can only recover it via `IsBernsteinFunction.continuousOn`, i.e. by supplying complete monotonicity it does not need. (The PR description claims reuse of `intervalIntegral.continuous_primitive`; it appears nowhere in the file.)

findings.evidence: Lines 146–148 prove the specialization from `isBernsteinFunction_const` + `.add` + `.congr`; `Basic.lean` lines 139–160 contain `add`/`smul` but no `const_add`.
findings.fix: Add `IsBernsteinFunction.const_add (hf) (hc : 0 ≤ c) : IsBernsteinFunction (fun t ↦ c + f t)` to `Basic.lean` next to `add`/`smul`, drop the two specialized `const_add_halfLinePrimitive` wrappers, or else also state the integral-form const-add so the doc matches the API.
findings.issue: `isBernsteinFunction_const_add_halfLinePrimitive` (and its `IsCompletelyMonotone` twin, line 168) is just `isBernsteinFunction_const.add … |>.congr rfl`; the reusable general lemma `IsBernsteinFunction.const_add` is missing from `Basic.lean`. Meanwhile the module doc (line 19) promises `t ↦ c + ∫₀ᵗ f` is Bernstein, but no lemma states the const-add case in integral form.

summary: `isBernsteinFunction_iff` and `IsBernsteinFunction.congr` are the right additions, but `halfLinePrimitive` ships without its defining equation or a standalone continuity lemma, so consumers cannot reason about it except through the full Bernstein conclusion. The const-add variants also duplicate `add` without a general closure lemma.
